items.label: KYB startup recall
items.copy:
the part about agents forgetting to query, i'd try a small startup briefing with active work + pointers, then fetch details as needed. thats the wakeup/recall loop in my backlog-mcp, might fit KYB too
https://github.com/gkoreli/backlog-mcp
items.fit: KYB's full article says agents can forget to call the memory tool and its described v0.3.3 lacks automatic startup context. The reply supplies backlog-mcp's bounded orientation/recall pattern, while recognizing KYB already handles record lifecycle and history.

items.label: AxiomCode exploration context
items.copy:
i'd keep the exploration transcript out of the main agent too, even a good map can turn into context spam. ghx keeps the recon session on disk, returns claims + file refs + uncertainty, you could put that boundary around graph queries too
https://github.com/gkoreli/ghx
items.fit: The thread describes repeated code rediscovery and links AxiomCode Graph. Its current default-branch README was read. The reply proposes an evidence-report boundary around graph exploration; it does not claim a reproduced flaw or measured context saving in AxiomCode.

items.label: Pankaj terminal input latency
items.copy:
that typing-delay row makes me want to check how work is chunked, in my ghostty-vt-js writes stay FIFO but yield between slices so input gets a turn. one huge chunk can still overrun it tho
https://github.com/gkoreli/ghostty-vt-js
items.fit: The author reports a terminal migration benchmark with a typing-delay row. The full post, replies and attached table were inspected. The reply shares ghostty-vt-js's FIFO time-sliced scheduling and single-chunk limitation; it does not assert that this fixes wterm or wins the benchmark.

items.label: Renée delegated agent permissions
items.copy:
this is the gap im working on with agentport, a site grants your own agent named tools for one session, with expiry and per-tool approvals. needs the site to opt in, but you dont have to hand the agent your login cookies
https://github.com/gkoreli/agentport
items.fit: The full post describes broken authorized sessions and explicitly asks for task-scoped, expiring permissions. The reply connects AgentPort's named site tools, session expiry and per-tool approvals to that gap, retaining the site opt-in requirement.

items.label: SEO Genius current experiment state
items.copy:
for that H1 example, i'd give each URL + field a stable key, with the test window attached. my backlog-mcp closes the old memory when a new one uses the same state_key, so you keep history without two current plans, thats the bit i'd borrow
https://github.com/gkoreli/backlog-mcp
items.fit: SEO Genius describes an agent prematurely rewriting an H1 and resetting an experiment. Existing replies already recommend a change ledger and observation window. This reply adds a concrete stable-key replacement mechanism from backlog-mcp, without assuming SEO Genius lacks one.
